T3. Forward-looking reporting long-term risks (next quarters/years) [YES] — BOJ rate path cadence, Japan fiscal trajectory, JGB yield pressure

**Synopsis:**
Treasury Secretary Bessent, speaking on the sidelines of the G20 in Asheville, downplayed current yen weakness as "well contained" and not disorderly — walking back the intervention-justifying language used after the July 31 joint US-Japan yen-buying operation. He signaled confidence in BOJ Governor Ueda to act appropriately, stopped short of prescribing aggressive hikes, but endorsed the view that Japan has exited deflation and Abenomics is effectively over. He framed Japan's current policy direction as "Takaichi-nomics" — more deregulatory and shareholder-friendly. Markets are nearly fully pricing a BOJ rate hike at the Sept 17-18 meeting. JGB 10-year yields have hit a three-decade high of 2.945%, driven partly by Takaichi's expansionary fiscal stance.
